definition: Formal reliability targets (availability, TTFT percentiles, tokens-per-second floors) adapted to AI's realities: provider outages, GPU shortages, nondeterministic quality.
details: Formal reliability targets (availability, TTFT percentiles, tokens-per-second floors) adapted to AI's realities: provider outages, GPU shortages, nondeterministic quality. Mature teams define quality SLOs (eval-score floors on live traffic samples), not just uptime.

explainer.lead: SLOs for AI systems are formal reliability targets adapted to AI's realities: provider outages, GPU shortages and nondeterministic quality. Mature teams also define quality SLOs, not just uptime.

tiers.eli5: It's a promise about how well a service will perform, like a delivery guarantee, but written knowing the kitchen sometimes runs out of ingredients.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set availability, TTFT percentile and tokens-per-second floor targets, and add eval-score floors measured on live traffic samples. A common pitfall is tracking only uptime while quality quietly degrades.
tiers.paperLevel: Targets are expressed as thresholds over metrics: availability, latency percentiles such as TTFT, tokens per second floors, and eval-score floors on sampled live traffic; because model outputs are nondeterministic, quality targets are statistical rather than exact.

explainer.example: A team commits to 99.5% availability, p95 TTFT under 800 ms and a minimum eval score on a weekly sample of live requests.
